stem: A client taking lisinopril develops sudden swelling of the lips and tongue. What is the priority interpretation and action?

options.A: This is an expected mild effect; continue the next dose and reassess tomorrow.
options.B: Suspect angioedema; stop lisinopril and obtain urgent evaluation of the airway.
options.C: Give the next lisinopril dose with food to reduce the swelling.
options.D: Treat the finding as isolated fluid retention and increase dietary sodium.

rationale: Lisinopril labeling warns that angioedema can occur and may involve the tongue, glottis, or larynx. The drug should be promptly discontinued and airway involvement requires urgent assessment and management.
educational_objective: Recognize ACE-inhibitor angioedema and the need to discontinue lisinopril and urgently assess airway compromise.
source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine
source_claim_supported: Lisinopril can cause angioedema involving the face, lips, tongue, glottis, or larynx; therapy should be promptly discontinued and airway compromise urgently managed.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
